## Interrogating Suspects
Security Personnel may choose to interrogate a suspect upon arresting them instead of detaining them in the brig. Interrogations can only be performed if the total sentencing time for the arresting crimes is above five minutes. Regardless of the duration of the original sentence, an Interrogation cannot exceed twenty minutes in length. **Interrogation fully replaces ordinary brigging time.** When the interrogation concludes, the suspect is immediately released, unless they would normally be brought to permanent confinement.
**The Head of Security or Warden must approve of any interrogation, and either of them can immediately end an interrogation at any time.**
The interrogation must take place inside of a secure and isolated area outside of the public eye, such as an interrogation room. During an interrogation, no more than three security personnel should be present. It is preferred if the officer that conducted the arrest be present for the interrogation. Any number of justice personnel may be present for the interrogation, but should try to not interfere with the interrogation. Prisoners being interrogated must be done individually, not as a group.
The interrogated person should be given basic food and water (or power, for synthetic suspects) upon request. The suspect must be cuffed to a chair or similar object for the full length of the interrogation. Security may choose to temporarily suspend medical care for the subject during the interrogation, but not to the point of the subject falling unconscious (see below).
Security is allowed and encouraged to cooperate with the suspect during the interrogation, such as dropping or changing a charge from the original sentence, providing specified “luxury” items, and other reasonable requests in exchange for helpful information. The Warden has the final say on accepting these exchanges, but is encouraged to do so.
-# Out of Character Note: Choosing to engage in more physical forms of interrogation should be done sparingly. When in doubt, seek out of character consent from all other players involved in LOOC.
Security personnel are allowed to physically encourage the suspect to answer questions, using only blunt or nonlethal instruments such as seclites and stun batons. Interrogating personnel should not be causing significant or disfiguring damage to the suspect during encouragement. If the subject is unconscious or dies at any point during the interrogation, the interrogation will immediately end, and medical aid must be given immediately. As soon as the interrogation is over, medical aid must be administered or requested as normal if the suspect has received any injuries.
## Do Not Resuscitate Orders
DNR (Do Not Resuscitate) orders should only be issued for suspects or criminals in times of significant stress upon the Security Department’s resources and personnel, or when the suspect in question has caused significant loss of life to station personnel. - “Significant stress” is determined by the Head of Security or, in times without a Head of Security, the Captain. - “Significant loss of life” is causing a Mass Casualty Event (as defined in Medical SOP), not simply the potential of such actions.
Do Not Resuscitate orders must be issued by the Head of Security or the Captain, and signed off on by either the Chief Medical Officer, or, in times without a CMO, the Captain. DNR orders must always be signed off on by someone other than the issuing Command member. If the Head of Security, CMO, and Captain are all unavailable, the Warden (or Corpsman, if the Warden is also unavailable) may temporarily authorize a DNR order. This “emergency” DNR must be reviewed and validated or revoked immediately as soon as the Captain or CMO are available.
When a DNR is issued for a suspect, if that suspect is killed in pursuit, during an arrest, or incidentally in any other way, Medical must not resuscitate them. - Instead, their body should be put into a body bag as soon as possible, and labeled with “[NAME OF DECEASED], DNR, DO NOT DISPOSE” - Alternatively, the Do Not Rescuscitate form may be directly attached to the body bag. - The body of the suspect must not be abused or tampered with in any way, by any personnel of any department. - It is critical that the body be prioritized for transport back to Central Command upon the end of shift or evacuation.
DNR orders must be faxed widely to medical, called out over Security comms, and, if possible (when the CMO signs the order), called out over medical comms.
## Treatment Upon Arrest
Upon detainment, and after sentencing, prisoners are to be moved to either the individual brig cells or permanent confinement (as the sentencing dictates).
The prisoner should first be searched. A search includes: - Bag - Any pockets of coat - Belt - Pockets of jumpsuit - Any containers within any of the aforementioned items or areas - Headsets (If the presence of stolen comms keys is suspected)
Searches do *not* include: - Implant searches (for which warrants are always required) - PDA searches (for which warrants are always required)
Move any contraband items to Evidence lockers (ideally in the armory). Move personal items that could pose a threat to the prisoner or security (including tools that could be used to escape) to Evidence lockers (ideally in proximity to the cell of the prisoner to be returned upon release).
Set the brig timer if not in permanent confinement.
Mark prisoner as “Detained” in the Security Records console if they have not already been marked so.
## Treatment Upon Release
Upon release from the brig, all personal items (but not contraband) are to be returned to the crew member. They should be shown out in a timely manner and without hostilities, and marked as “released” in the Security Records console.
## Treatment of Prisoners
Prisoners—both those confined to the brig for crimes committed on shift, and those in permanent confinement—are guaranteed the following, irrevocable rights: - Adequate medical care - This includes prescription medications. If these prescription medications are controlled substances, medical staff should be brought in to supervise medication dosage, but this dosage must not be denied. - Psychological counseling (if there is a psychologist or other trained and willing member of the Medical Department available) - Spiritual counseling (if there is a chaplain or other trained and willing member of the Epistemics Department available) - Legal counseling (ideally from the Justice Department; Security, however, must be willing to provide what legal counsel they can if there is no Justice Department available) - Food and water of the appropriate (digestible and non-toxic) type for organic prisoners - Accessible Electrical Power (typically an APC) for synthetic prisoners. - Synthetic prisoners should be provided with upgraded power cells upon request, provided such power cells are 1) available to the rest of the station and 2) the station has adequate materials to reasonably supply such power cells. - Microreactors and similar “self-recharging” energy sources may be provided to synthetic prisoners with the Warden’s (or, in circumstances without a warden, the Head of Security’s, Chief Justice’s, or the Captain’s) explicit permission. - Prisoner clothing (jumpsuit and shoes at minimum) - Safety within the brig or permanent confinement area from: - Spacings - Hostile entities - Inhospitable temperatures - Toxic atmosphere - Hostile actors, both crew and non crew - Physical and metaphysical anomalies - Under non-emergency conditions, Epistemics should be given time and resources required to move such anomalies, should the Mystagogue or Captain deem it appropriate for the station’s research goals. - If Epistemics can reliably prove that an anomaly is not a hazard to the prisoners (including reasonable modifications to the confinement area, such as adding windows to prevent direct physical contact with the anomaly), the anomaly should not be considered a hazard. - The anomaly containment must be approved by the Warden. - If the Warden is skeptical of the integrity of the anomaly containment setup, they must call for engineering to verify the safety of the containment. - Under emergency conditions, the Warden (or, in circumstances where there is no warden or the warden is not available in a reasonable time, the Head of Security, Chief Justice, or Captain) has license to instruct Epistemics to immediately dispatch of the anomaly. - The Warden (or other authority mentioned above) has the final say in whether a situation constitutes “emergency conditions” for anomaly removal. Prisoners are guaranteed the following rights that can be revoked upon reasonable threat to prisoner safety, security safety, or flight risk. - Freedom of movement within either their cell (for prisoners held in the brig) or the designated permanent confinement area (for prisoners upon shift start or confined to permanent confinement for the rest of shift) - Confiscated items should be returned upon request from arrested prisoners so long as they do not pose an undue threat or are contraband. - If there is a dispute over what is an “undue” threat, the warden has final say. - Likewise, reasonable requests from prisoners should be honored. - If there is a dispute over what is a “reasonable” request, the warden has final say. - Prisoners should have access to common and prison comms unless they become unduly disruptive. - If there is a dispute over what is “unduly” disruptive, the warden has final say. - Prisoners in permanent confinement should be allowed visitors (per the Visitation Policy) so long as the visitors comply with the Visitation Policy. - If there is dispute over what constitutes “reasonable” threat to prisoner safety, security safety, or flight risk, the warden has final say.
## Visitation Policy
Prisoners in permanent confinement have the right to visitation. This right can be revoked by the Warden or Head of Security in the case of unduly disruptive prisoners, or a demonstrated history of problems with visitors for a specific prisoner. - Visitation may be requested by the prisoner or by other people who wish to visit the prisoner. - Generally, prisoners should not be allowed multiple visitors at a time. The Warden or Head of Security can make an exception for this if they so desire, and are encouraged to do so in the cases of prisoners who demonstrate good behavior. - Prisoners must fill out the Visitation Form, which must be available upon request at Security. The Visitation form must have the following information: - The name of the prisoner being visited, and if they consent to being visited. - The name of the visitor, and if they agree to visit. - The name of the Warden when the form was created. - If there is no Warden available, the name of the Head of Security should be used. - The Visitation form must be reviewed by the Warden (or, in circumstances without a Warden, the Head of Security, the Captain, or the Chief Justice). - Upon review, a copy of the form is to be given to the prisoner and visitor specified. - If they consent to visitation, the visitor is to be escorted into security and given a full search. - All weapons and tools, even legal ones (such as kitchen knives, box cutters, power drills, crowbars, etc), must be held in security, outside of permanent confinement, until the visitation is concluded (at which point legal items should be returned). - No contraband may enter permanent confinement. - Alcohol and other mind-altering substances require approval from the individual who reviewed the initial visitation form. They can be denied for any reason. - Visitation is not time restricted. - Security can order the visitor to leave at any time, for any reason, including: - Safety threat to permanent confinement - Unruly or intimidating behavior from any prisoner or visitor - Medical emergencies of any prisoner or visitor - Conjugal visits to permanent confinement prisoners are allowed, and need not be specified on the visitation form. The prisoner should, however, use prison comms to make it clear to Security that they are privately occupied (and not in danger) to avoid undue concern if or when security cannot locate them easily in permanent confinement during a conjugal visit.
## Solitary Confinement
Solitary Confinement is always a temporary measure on station which should never exceed twenty minutes. During Solitary Confinement, prisoners retain all of their irrevocable rights as prisoners (listed above: in summary, medical care, counseling from appropriate individuals, food, water, power for silicons, clothing, and safety). They are not allowed comms or visitors for the duration of Solitary Confinement. Prisoners in Solitary Confinement must be separated from other prisoners. (Many station models are not set up to accommodate Solitary Confinement. Consult the Engineering Department for assistance.)
Solitary Confinement should not be used as a coercive threat, but rather as a protective measure.
## Stasis
In the event that a prisoner cannot be reasonably held in the brig or permanent confinement by Security (either from their demonstrated abilities and/or skills, or due to lack of manpower in Security), Security can put the prisoner into stasis. **Stasis is defined as humanely executing a prisoner for the explicit purpose of reviving them at Central Command for transfer to a facility that can hold them.**
**Stasis cannot be used as a punishment for crimes on its own.** It is not a form of punishment; it is a form of containment.
Stasis follows these guidelines: - The Head of Security, Captain, or Chief Justice must give consent for the prisoner to be put into stasis. While the Warden is well within their right to make recommendations for stasis, if at all possible, the Head of Security, Captain, or Chief Justice must also sign off on the order. If the Captain, Head of Security, and Chief Justice are all incapable of responding, the Warden may place the prisoner into stasis temporarily. This “emergency” stasis must be reviewed and validated or revoked immediately as soon as the Captain, Head of Security, or Chief Justice are present. - Any member of Security can carry out the order of stasis, provided they follow all requirements for equipment and other personnel per the method chosen. However, stasis can only be carried out via the following methods: - Lethal injection - Medical should prepare 45 units of Heartbreaker Toxin, and medical or the corpsman should inject all 45 units into the prisoner in quick succession to ensure efficient, humane execution. - Electrocution - Engineering should be contacted to construct a high-voltage electric grille in a secure area. A security officer with insulated gloves must push the prisoner into the grille until they are dead, and then the grille should be immediately deconstructed or de-powered. This process should not be automated to prevent excessive damage to the body. - Spacing - Since body preservation is critical to stasis, it is important that the prisoner to be put in stasis is not allowed to drift off into space. This can be done by a chamber constructed by engineering, or by cuffing the prisoner to a chair. - The prisoner to be put into stasis can choose which of these methods they prefer. If they refuse to choose, or their choice cannot be carried out expediently for whatever reason, the Warden or Head of Security must choose one of the other options for them. - Under no circumstances should a prisoner be executed in any other way, even upon prisoner request. - All executions for stasis must be done in private, and away from public view. Only the Security and Justice departments should be in attendance, with required engineering or medical where necessary. The prisoner must also be informed of the following: - Upon prisoner request, the chaplain and/or psychologist may be in attendance. - Upon prisoner request, gaseous Nitrous Oxide may be provided to safely render them unconscious for the process. - Medical must be informed of the incoming body for stasis before the execution takes place. - A body bag should be immediately available for after the execution, and obtained before the execution takes place. - The body of the prisoner to be put in stasis should be immediately transferred into the body bag, labeled with “[NAME OF PRISONER], STASIS, DO NOT DISPOSE] or have the Stasis Order paper directly attached to it, and transported to the morgue or corpsman’s room. The bodies must remain in the body bags, and must not be transferred into the morgue slabs. - The body of the prisoner must not be abused or tampered with in any way, by any personnel of any department. - It is critical that the body be prioritized for transport back to Central Command upon end of shift or evacuation.
